notFormalized.title: Proposition 10.1.9, (LR) under equivalences
notFormalized.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.9, p. 468 (new in the 2021 edition)

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.2.2: the structures induced from the triple products

notFormalized.title: Remark 10.3.18: generalized isomorphisms with $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$ are not unique
notFormalized.label: §10.3, Remark 10.3.18, pp. 492–493 (2017: Remark 10.3, p. 355), the non-uniqueness of $f$
notFormalized.book: A generalized isomorphism $f$ with $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$ is in general not unique.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.60), by the example of Remark 10.5.5: the base classes of $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ are two distinct generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map, so with $\beta' = \beta \circ |f|^{-1}$ both satisfy $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$; the relation itself is V10.48 (Findings, Chapter 10, items 39, 56).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.3.19, generalized isomorphisms are determined by their orbit maps under (LR)
notFormalized.label: §10.3, Theorem 10.3.19, p. 493 (2017: Theorem 10.7, p. 355)
notFormalized.book: If one of $X$, $Y$ has (LR) and $f, f' : X \to Y$ are generalized isomorphisms with $|f| = |f'|$, then $f = f'$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.65, V10.66), as a statement that does not hold as we read it: on $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action, which has (LR), two generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map differ; the proof's step on p. 494 uses the families $\alpha_a$ of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) as a natural transformation, which in the example none is. With $Y$ effective the theorem holds (V10.66) (Findings, Chapter 10, items 17, 39, 58).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.4.5, the Fred part
notFormalized.label: §10.4, Theorem 10.4.5, p. 501 (2017: Theorem 10.8, p. 362), the sc-Fredholm section functors
notFormalized.book: $\Phi_*$ and $\Phi^*$ map sc-Fredholm section functors to sc-Fredholm section functors.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.27). $\Phi_*$ and $\Phi^*$ map sc-Fredholm section functors to sc-Fredholm section functors and restrict to mutually inverse bijections of $\mathrm{Fred}$ (`theorem_10_4_5_fred`). The invariance it needed is proved: a local strong bundle isomorphism (`StrongBundle.LocalIso`) carries sc-Fredholm germs to sc-Fredholm germs, read in the transported chart (`LocalIso.isScFredholmGerm`, `transportChart`, `isChart_transportChart`), so Definition 3.1.18 is local (`isScFredholmSection_of_forall`, `Chapter3/FredholmPullbackIso.lean`), and the action of a morphism is such an isomorphism (`exists_localIso_mor`, `Chapter10/FredholmEquivalence.lean`) (Findings, Chapter 10, item 44).

notFormalized.title: Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7, (LR) and natural families for strong bundles
notFormalized.label: §10.4, Proposition 10.4.6, p. 501 (new in the 2021 edition), and Proposition 10.4.7, pp. 501–502 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The local regularity property of strong bundles is invariant under strong bundle equivalences (proof left to the reader), and the strong bundle version of Proposition 10.1.10.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the ep-groupoid versions are formalized since (V10.62, V10.63); the strong bundle versions need the transport $H_{\hat\psi}$ as a strong bundle isomorphism at levels $0$ and $1$ and the inverse of a strong bundle isomorphism on an open set, which the strong bundle API does not provide (Findings, Chapter 10, item 45).

notFormalized.title: the transitivity of the equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles, the composition in $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ and the strong bundle version of Theorem 10.3.10
notFormalized.label: §10.5, p. 504 (2017 p. 364), Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366), and Remark 10.5.3, p. 506 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles is an equivalence relation, generalized strong bundle maps compose to a category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$, and a generalized strong bundle map is invertible iff it is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.68–V10.71), except the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10. The weak fibred product of strong bundles is the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$ (V10.68), the equivalence of diagrams is transitive (V10.69), and the composition makes $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ a category (V10.70, V10.55); a diagram with both legs strong bundle equivalences represents an isomorphism (V10.71). Still open: that an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences, proved for the base functor only; for the strong bundle functor it would need strong bundle versions of the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2 (Findings, Chapter 10, items 18, 19, 50, 53).

notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the text uses no property of them, and $q$, $Q$ depend on the representative; the homomorphism $\gamma$ is formalized (V10.54) (Findings, Chapter 10, items 51, 52).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.5.7, generalized strong bundle isomorphisms determined by their orbit maps
notFormalized.label: §10.5, Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10, p. 367)
notFormalized.book: If both strong bundles have the local regularity property and $[D], [D']$ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with $|[D]| = |[D']|$, then $[D] = [D']$.
